market.question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the October 2026 meeting?
market.rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's October 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for October 27-28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their October meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

market.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by October 31, 2026?
market.rules:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

recent_facts.fact: As of the October 2 update, the US blockade of Iranian ports was still in force. Trump said on September 30 that the US had 'virtually total control', which has not been verified. The update also says no active ceasefire negotiations were confirmed as of October 3 and that Qatar is still mediating.

On October 1, Trump rejected Iran's seven-day proposal and insisted that nuclear issues be dealt with first. Iran had offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for the release of about $12 billion in frozen assets, the lifting of oil sanctions and an end to the US blockade.

A source told The National that Iran is preparing for a 'major round of fighting'. Several meetings in New York last month ended without a breakthrough, and both Trump and Iranian officials have signaled they are getting ready for the war to resume. Araghchi said Iran would fight even if it meant an 'apocalyptic' war.

Trump called the Iranian plan 'unacceptable' and described the blockade as 'the greatest blockade in military history -- it's a wall of steel'. The US sent a counterproposal. The two sides disagree on sequencing: Iran wants the US to act first, and Washington wants Iran to reopen the strait first.

Officials said mediators were working on a framework with these terms: reopen the strait with no tolls, lift the US blockade first, remove sanctions afterward, and include Iranian nuclear concessions and inspector access. Officials also said the US had not formally rejected the proposal and that Trump's public rejection may have been a negotiating tactic. Indirect talks were expected to resume on Monday, September 28.

Trump said he expected negotiations with Iran that week even though he had rejected Iran's latest proposal. That proposal was conveyed in indirect talks in New York and tied reopening Hormuz to lifting the blockade, oil-sanctions relief and a regional ceasefire.
Iran loaded no crude onto tankers in September 2026, down from about 250,000 barrels per day in August, because of the US blockade.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States naval blockade of Iran)
recent_facts.fact: The second phase of the blockade started on July 14, 2026 and is still going on. By September 12, more than 100 ships had been redirected, and several vessels had been disabled, including Belma, Lavine and Vela Nova. The article says the blockade has completely stopped new Iranian oil exports from the Gulf.

Trump said strikes could resume after the November 3 midterm elections 'if negotiations fail'. A third carrier strike group, USS Theodore Roosevelt, is heading to the CENTCOM area. No formal talks with a fixed date before October 15 were found.

Iran dismissed a 15-point US plan covering sanctions relief, nuclear rollback, missile limits and reopening Hormuz. Iran's counterproposal demands war reparations, guarantees against future war and Iranian sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz.

Precedent: the first phase of the blockade ran from April 13 to June 18, 2026, about 66 days. It was lifted the same day a US-Iran memorandum was signed (at Versailles), which extended the ceasefire and started a 60-day negotiation clock. Lifting the blockade was announced at the time the deal took effect.

Trump announced the blockade was being reinstated on July 13, less than a month into the June ceasefire. This followed Iranian attacks on commercial ships in Hormuz starting July 7, and enforcement resumed July 14. Unverified count from this research: the US has announced an end to the blockade once (June 18) and reinstated it once.

market.question: Israel accuses Iran/proxies of plane stabbing incident by Oct 31?
market.rules:
On September 30, 2026, FlyDubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv diverted to Saudi Arabia following an incident in the cockpit in which the co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain. (see: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/diverted-flydubai-flight-israel-was-not-hijacking-incident-israeli-prime-2026-09-30/).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Israeli national government, or an authorized representative of the Israeli national government, publicly announces that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused this incident, by October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A public announcement refers to an on-the-record statement issued by the Israeli national government or by its authorized representatives acting in an official capacity on behalf of the Israeli national government. A statement or press release issued by the Israeli national government or any of its agencies will qualify. A Prime Minister or Cabinet Minister’s public statements will always be considered to be issued on-the-record in a capacity representing the Israeli national government for purposes of this market. A statement from a lawmaker or other government official speaking in their own capacity or on behalf of a party not in government will not alone qualify.

For purposes of this market, an affiliated group of Iran is: any organization directly controlled by Iran, Hezbollah, Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, Houthis ("Ansar Allah"), Kata'ib Hezbollah, Asa'ib Ahl al-Haq, Badr Organization, and Harakat al-Nujaba. An unlisted group will only qualify if the Israeli claim itself, or accompanying statements or releases, specifies that the group is a proxy of or otherwise is controlled or directed by Iran. A general statement that it was conducted by an Iranian proxy will also qualify, even if no group is named.

Such a statement will be considered to claim that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused the incident if it explicitly claims that Iran or an affiliated group ordered, carried out, planned, or otherwise directly aided or coordinated the incident. Statements that attribute only inspiration or ideological influence (e.g., "this would not have happened if Iran didn't radicalize terrorists," "the co-pilot was influenced by Hamas' ideas") will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement has been made, no subsequent walkback or retraction will be relevant for purposes of this market. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Israeli national government; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.fact: Asked whether Iran was linked to the FlyDubai FZ1073 attack, Prime Minister Netanyahu said: "It's too early to say. The attacking pilot is now being investigated in Saudi Arabia." He said questioning had shown the co-pilot "underwent Islamist radical indoctrination."

A senior Israeli official said the co-pilot most likely acted alone. Two Israeli security officials told Reuters that no evidence of Iranian involvement had been found so far, and the initial assessment was that he acted independently. The investigation is still open.

Despite Trump's remarks, a senior Israeli official said on Thursday that investigators have so far ruled out an apparent connection to Iran. Reports describe a growing assessment that he acted alone for nationalist reasons. That assessment has not been confirmed.

Trump said he had reason to believe Iran was involved: "Based on what I'm hearing is yes, but we're working on it right now." Israeli officials said they currently have no indications of Iranian involvement but have not ruled it out.

Trump said the US would strike Iran "very hard" if a Tehran link were established, but he made no definitive accusation. market.question: Next US-Iran senior diplomatic meeting by October 31, 2026? (copy)
market.rules:
On September 22, U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, with President Trump saying another meeting is scheduled in the near future.(see: https://www.israelhayom.com/2026/09/22/witkoff-kushner-attended-us-iran-meeting-another-expected-soon). 

This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is a direct or indirect senior-level diplomatic meeting between the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A diplomatic meeting occurs when representatives of both listed countries who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to engage in diplomacy on behalf of their respective governments or governing authorities deliberately meet for the purpose of diplomacy or negotiation. A qualifying meeting need not result in any agreement, joint statement, or further engagement.

A diplomatic meeting is senior-level if each listed entity is represented by a head of state, a head of government, or a vice president; a foreign minister; a minister of cabinet rank; the secretary or head of a national security council; the presiding officer of a national legislature; a special envoy; or another individual designated by the head of state or head of government to conduct diplomatic negotiations on their behalf. Individuals authorized only for technical, implementation, monitoring, staff-level, preparatory, or working-group-level talks will not be considered designated to conduct diplomatic negotiations on behalf of the head of state or head of government. This definition includes, but is not limited to, all of the following individuals: for the United States, Donald Trump, JD Vance, Marco Rubio, Scott Bessent, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner; and for Iran, Mojtaba Khamenei, Masoud Pezeshkian, Abbas Araghchi and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf. In each case, a qualifying representative must participate in the meeting.

A direct meeting refers to a diplomatic meeting where the representatives of both countries directly interact with each other in person. Meetings conducted through translators qualify, provided direct, face-to-face communication occurs. An indirect meeting refers to a meeting conducted indirectly through designated mediators or facilitators. A qualifying indirect meeting must meet both of the following criteria (i) the designated intermediaries act with the knowledge and authorization of both entities; (ii) representatives of both entities are physically present in the same facility, venue, or city as part of a single organized round of talks convened for the purpose of diplomatic engagement, with the intermediary conveying communications between the representatives or delegations on the same day. “The same day” means the same calendar day local time at the meeting location.

Sessions, proceedings, or convenings of standing international organizations, treaty bodies, or recurring multilateral summits or conferences (e.g., the United Nations General Assembly, G7, and G20 summits) do not qualify, unless a qualifying and deliberate diplomatic meeting between representatives of the listed countries is separately held alongside such a convening.

The following do not qualify as either a direct or indirect diplomatic meeting: chance encounters; standalone exchanges limited to greetings, courtesies, or photo opportunities; meetings conducted remotely, by telephone, or by any other means where the relevant representatives are not physically present at the same facility, venue, or city on the same day; discussions involving persons not authorized to engage in diplomacy or negotiation on behalf of their respective governments.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

Dallas's defense has given up 539 rushing yards, 31st in the NFL, and has only two sacks in three games.

Dallas leads the all-time series 4-3 over 7 meetings, a small sample; this is the eighth. Houston's three wins came at home in 2002 and 2018 and in Dallas in 2024.
Against Indianapolis, C.J. Stroud went 8-of-10 for 114 yards in the fourth quarter, with five completions of 15+ yards, in a game where the offense otherwise struggled.

Tournament Winner and End of Round Leader markets will resolve to No

recent_facts.fact: After 36 holes Austin Smotherman leads at 17-under 125 (rounds of 63-62), one shot ahead of Kevin Roy (-16). Doug Ghim and Kevin Streelman are T3 at -15, Stephan Jaeger is 5th at -14, Steven Fisk 6th at -13, and Michael Brennan and Neal Shipley are T7 at -12.
Smotherman's second-round 62 included 10 birdies and matched his career-low round. His 125 set the tournament's 36-hole record. This is his 100th PGA Tour start and he has never won on Tour.

The 2026 Bank of Utah Championship runs Oct. 1-4 at Black Desert Resort in Ivins, Utah (par 71, 7,421 yards) with a 120-player field, a $6 million purse and 500 FedExCup points. The final round is Sunday, Oct. 4, well before the question closes on Oct. 18.
Smotherman and Kevin Roy are the final pairing for Saturday's third round (Oct. 3), with Streelman and Ghim in the group ahead. No third-round results had been published when searched on 2026-10-03.

Earlier in 2026 Smotherman held his first PGA Tour 36-hole lead, by three shots after opening 62-69 at the Cognizant Classic. He finished T2 there and did not win (date approximate: Cognizant Classic weekend in early March).

Kevin Roy, second at -16, opened with two 63s, beating his previous best 36-hole total by five shots. Doug Ghim shot a bogey-free 62 in round 2. Conditions were described as perfect, and Tony Finau missed the cut.
The question resolves Yes only if Smotherman wins the tournament outright, including any playoff. A withdrawal or forfeit resolves No for the Tournament Winner market.
The event is a 72-hole stroke-play tournament with a 36-hole cut. A tie after 72 holes is settled by a sudden-death playoff, so there is always a single winner.

This market will resolve based on the company that occupies first place under this ranking.

If this resolution source is unavailable at check time, this market will remain open until the leaderboard comes back online and will resolve based on the first check after it becomes available. If it becomes permanently unavailable, this market will resolve to "Other".

recent_facts.fact: USA vs Mexico kicks off October 3, 2026 at 7 p.m. MT (02:00 UTC October 4) at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona, so the USA is at home. It was the second-to-last match of the USMNT's four-game fall window, and Canada is next.

The USA beat Chile 4-2 on September 29, 2026 in St. Louis. That followed a 4-1 win over Peru on September 26 in Orlando, which gave them back-to-back four-goal wins under Mauricio Pochettino with a very young squad.

Mexico drew Peru 1-1 on September 29, 2026 in Harrison, NJ. Peru led from the 26th minute and Víctor Guzmán equalized in the 49th. It was Mexico's second straight 1-1 draw under new coach Rafael Márquez, after drawing 1-1 with Colombia on September 26.
Mexico fielded a young lineup with several debutants against Peru. Rafael Márquez took over as head coach after the 2026 World Cup, and these are his first matches in charge.
Mexico's window is Colombia (Sep 26, Baltimore), Peru (Sep 29, NJ), USA (Oct 3, Arizona) and Chile (Oct 6, Los Angeles). That means three games in eight days, with Chile three days after this match.
The all-time series is USA 24 wins, Mexico 38, draws 17. Since 2021 the USA is 5-2-2 against Mexico, but Mexico won the most recent meeting 2-1 in the Gold Cup Final on July 6, 2025.
In 46 meetings on U.S. soil, the USA has won 21, Mexico 13, with 12 draws: Mexico won about 28% and 26% were draws.

recent_facts.fact: August 2026 CPI-U rose 3.4% over 12 months before seasonal adjustment, the same as in July. The NSA index was 334.980, against 323.976 in August 2025. The seasonally adjusted monthly change was +0.4%.

recent_facts.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (via DOL)
recent_facts.fact: The September 2025 CPI-U NSA index was 324.800, up 3.0% y/y. That puts the Aug-to-Sep 2025 NSA rise at about +0.25%, from 323.976. This is the base the September 2026 y/y figure is measured against.

recent_facts.source: Derived arithmetic from BLS index levels
recent_facts.fact: For the published y/y to round to 3.7% or higher, the September 2026 NSA index must exceed about 336.655 (324.800 × 1.0365). That requires an Aug-to-Sep 2026 NSA rise of about +0.50% from 334.980. A rise of about +0.40% (index about 336.33) would give roughly 3.55–3.6%. A rise near +0.25%, the same as last September, would leave y/y near 3.4%.
Gasoline accounted for over one third of the 0.4% monthly all-items increase in August 2026.
EIA monthly average U.S. regular retail gasoline: June 2026 $4.050, July $3.932, August $4.058, September $4.355. That makes September about 7.3% above August.

AAA's September 2026 monthly average gas price was $4.33, a record for September and 50 cents above the previous record of $3.83 set in 2023. The national average was $4.41 on Oct 1, down nearly 7 cents in a week, and crude was in the $90/barrel range.
AAA's national average climbed through September 2026: $4.14 on Sep 3, $4.27 on Sep 10, $4.43 on Sep 17 and $4.48 on Sep 24, the highest ever for that time of year.

AAA reported August 2026 as the most expensive August on record, with the national average above $4 every day. The mid-month August average was $4.06, and a secondary summary gave $4.19 for the full month; the two AAA-derived figures disagree, so this one is unverified.
September 2026 CPI is scheduled for release on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET, which is 12:30 UTC. The question closes at 12:29 UTC that day.
The question resolves on the one-decimal 12-month NSA all-items CPI-U change BLS reports for September 2026. It must be strictly above 3.6%, so 3.6% resolves No and 3.7% or higher resolves Yes.

market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the first round of the next Brazil Presidential Election.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the vote count has been made official.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

market.question: When will Anthropic officially announce an IPO? (Before Nov 1, 2026)
market.rules:
If Anthropic confirms an IPO before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
An IPO is confirmed if 1) the SEC declares the company's Form S-1 effective OR 2) the IPO is priced OR 3) a securities exchange has assigned a ticker to it. As long as any of those events occur, the market will immediately resolve to Yes, even if the company does not start trading until after Nov 1, 2026.

recent_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported that after delays, Anthropic is aiming to complete its IPO before the Thanksgiving holiday, which falls on 2026-11-26, and to list in November.

Anthropic reportedly aims to go public as soon as mid-November 2026. It could start marketing the IPO the week of November 9, with investor meetings reported for October 14. The ticker shown, ANTH.PVT, is Yahoo's label for a private company, not one assigned by an exchange.
As of September 15, 2026, the tracker listed no public S-1 on EDGAR, no pricing date and no ticker assigned. It said the roadshow was expected in mid-October at the earliest.

Reuters read Anthropic's IPO prospectus and reported its contents, including a 2025 net loss and an existential-risk warning. Several outlets, including CNN, Fortune and Gizmodo, describe it as a 'leaked' prospectus, which suggests it was not a public EDGAR filing.
Fortune called the S-1 prospectus 'leaked'. The reported document runs 261 pages, about 80 of them on risk factors.
Reports say Anthropic picked Nasdaq, with Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan as lead underwriters. Anthropic has not confirmed a ticker or an official IPO date.

Reuters reported the IPO launch had moved toward mid-October at the earliest, with timing subject to change. Later reports said the listing was pushed to November so the offering could include third-quarter results.

SEC rules require a company that filed confidentially to file its registration statement publicly at least 15 days before the roadshow starts. Pricing and the SEC declaring the S-1 effective usually come at the end of the roadshow.
On June 1, 2026, Anthropic confirmed it had confidentially submitted a draft S-1 to the SEC. The number of shares and the price were not set.

The question resolves Yes only if, before Nov 1, 2026, the SEC declares the S-1 effective, the IPO is priced, or an exchange assigns a ticker. A ticker shown on an aggregator site, such as 'ANTP' on Investing.com, is unofficial according to the tracker.

Wild Card results: the White Sox swept the Astros 2-0 and the Yankees swept the Red Sox 2-0 in the AL. In the NL, the Braves beat the Phillies 2-1 and the Padres swept the Cubs 2-0. The other teams with byes are the Rays (AL No. 1), Dodgers and Brewers.
Chicago won the regular-season series against Cleveland 7-6. These two teams have never met in the postseason before.

ALDS schedule: Game 1 is in Cleveland on Oct 3 at 1 p.m. ET and Game 2 is in Cleveland on Oct 5. Game 3 is in Chicago on Oct 7, and Game 4 (if needed) is in Chicago on Oct 8. Game 5 (if needed) is back in Cleveland on Oct 10.

Rookie left-hander Parker Messick starts Game 1 for Cleveland and Gavin Williams starts Game 2. Chicago starts rookie left-hander Hagen Smith in Game 1. No Game 1 result was available when this was researched.

To win the title, Cleveland would have to win three more rounds: the best-of-five ALDS, the best-of-seven ALCS against the Rays or the Yankees, and the best-of-seven World Series. All of these are due to finish before the question closes on Oct 31.
Under the 12-team format from 2022 to 2024, 6 of the 12 teams with byes lost in the Division Series and 3 lost in the LCS. One lost the World Series and 2 won it (2022 Astros, 2024 Dodgers).

In 2025, 3 of the 4 teams with byes won their Division Series (Brewers, Mariners, Blue Jays). That makes roughly 9 of 16 bye teams winning the DS since 2022. The 2025 champion Dodgers did not have a bye, so 2 of 16 bye teams went on to win the World Series. The 2025 part of this count and the 2025 champion come from memory and are unverified.

market.question: Will ACM Neto win the 2026 Bahia gubernatorial election?
market.rules:
The Bahia gubernatorial election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026, with a runoff on October 25, 2026, if no candidate receives a majority of the valid votes in the first round.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

Temporary, interim, or placeholder governors appointed by any means before the specified election will not be considered.

If the result of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., www.tse.jus.br/eleicoes/resultados-eleicoes).

recent_facts.fact: In AtlasIntel's poll (2,000 voters, Sept 24–28, margin ±2 pts), Jerônimo Rodrigues (PT) had 50.7% of valid votes and ACM Neto (União Brasil) 47.5%. In the runoff scenario it was Jerônimo 51.4%, ACM Neto 48.6%.
AtlasIntel's previous poll (1,804 respondents, Aug 28–Sept 2) had ACM Neto at 49.1% and Jerônimo at 47.9%. Jerônimo moved ahead in AtlasIntel's next poll at the end of September.

Real Time Big Data (1,600 voters, Sept 23–26, ±2 pts) had Jerônimo at 47% and ACM Neto at 43% when voters were shown the candidate list, which is 51% to 47% of valid votes. In the runoff scenario it was Jerônimo 48%, ACM Neto 44%.

Quaest (900 voters, Sept 20–23, ±3 pts, registration BA-01850/2026) had ACM Neto at 42% and Jerônimo at 40%. Quaest's previous round had them at 44% and 41%. In the runoff scenario it was ACM Neto 45%, Jerônimo 43%, and 79% of respondents said their choice was final.
Paraná Pesquisas (released Sept 24) had ACM Neto at 46.7% and Jerônimo at 42% in the first round. A CNN Brasil report on Paraná Pesquisas gives a runoff of ACM Neto 48.4%, Jerônimo 44.2%.
Veritá (2,020 voters, Sept 20–24, ±2.5 pts) had ACM Neto at 51.1% of valid votes and Jerônimo at 47.7%.
Futura Inteligência/Política Livre had ACM Neto at 51.3% and Jerônimo at 43.6%, a gap of 7.7 points.

The two most recent polls (Real Time Big Data and AtlasIntel) both show incumbent Jerônimo Rodrigues numerically ahead. The four polls released in the last week of September all showed a technical tie within the margin of error.

Nine more Bahia governor polls are registered for release. On Oct 2: 100% Cidades, Veritá and Publivende. On Oct 3: Quaest, AtlasIntel, Instituto Franca, Paraná Pesquisas, DataTrends and Datasensus. The first round is Oct 4, 2026, with a runoff on Oct 25 if no one wins a majority of valid votes.

In 2022 Jerônimo led the first round with 49.45% to ACM Neto's 40.80%, even though most registered polls had shown Neto leading or winning outright. Jerônimo then won the runoff 52.79% (4,480,464 votes) to 47.21% (4,007,023).

In 2022, AtlasIntel's late-July/early-August Bahia poll was the one that showed a technical tie between Jerônimo and Neto, while other pollsters had Neto well ahead. That is a single-case observation of pollster accuracy, so treat it as unverified evidence.
The same Real Time Big Data release reported Lula above 60% in Bahia. Jerônimo is the PT incumbent and Lula's ally in the state.

MrBeast posted a video about spending $10M to build a village (Abna Dakwa) in Ghana. He said viewers engage less with philanthropy videos but that he will keep making them.

It had 87.61 million total views about 10 days and 7 hours after upload, so its 7-day total was below 87.6M, most likely somewhere in the 80–87M range. recent_facts.fact: As of 2026-10-03, no main video after 2026-09-19 turned up in the searches. Known 2026 uploads include April 4, June 27, an August video, and September 19, which suggests main uploads come roughly every 2–4 weeks rather than weekly. The questions close 2026-10-11. If no video is posted by 2026-10-31, they resolve to the lowest bracket.
"50 Streamers Fight for $1,000,000," uploaded 2026-04-04, got about 80.6 million views in its first week: 37M in 24 hours and 51M by day two. This is unverified because the page returned 403.
UNILAD Tech says MrBeast's videos now typically settle at around 60–90 million views, down from earlier levels of 150–200 million.

From 2026-08-24, YouTube counts a view as soon as a video starts playing, with no 30-second minimum. This could raise public view counts compared with earlier videos. The article does not make clear whether the change covers long-form videos or only Shorts.
A MrBeast video from around May–June 2026 got 25–30 million views on day one, according to the resolved result reported on this page. The exact video and date are unverified.
"Survive 30 Days Chained To A Stranger, Win $250,000" was uploaded 2026-06-27. No week-1 view count was found for it.

Tubefilter tracked MrBeast's branded videos in September 2026. Third-party data showed the whole channel adding about 44–71 million views a day in early September, with a spike of about 224 million on 2026-09-10. These are channel totals, not views for a single video.
MrBeast passed 500 million YouTube subscribers on 2026-06-12. Later 2026 stats put the channel at about 519 million subscribers and 141 billion total views.

Earlier MrBeast videos had much bigger openings: "$1 vs $250,000 Vacation" got 52M views in 24 hours and about 90M within a few days, and "$1 vs $1,000,000,000 Yacht" got 47M in 24 hours. Both are from before 2026, so they may not reflect current performance.

If the game is canceled entirely, with no make-up game, this market will resolve "No".

The primary resolution source for this market is the official statistics of the event as recognized by the governing body or event organizers. However, if the governing body or event organizers have not published final match statistics within 2 hours after the event's conclusion, data from Flashscore may be used; if Flashscore data is unavailable, data from Sofascore may be used; if neither is available, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead. All markets will settle based on the official final result as recognized by the governing body or event organizers. Revisions to officially declared final scores made after market resolution will not be accounted for in determining the outcome. If no acceptable data is available within 24 hours of the event's conclusion, this market will resolve 50-50, or to "Draw" where applicable.

Portugal host Norway in UEFA Nations League A, Group A4 on Sunday, October 4 at Estádio do Dragão in Porto, kicking off at 8:45pm local (18:45 GMT). Goal.com lists 13:45 GMT instead, so the two sources disagree on the kickoff time.
Group A4 table after 3 matchdays: Portugal 9 pts (3W, goals 7-3); Denmark, Norway and Wales 3 pts each. Norway are 1W-2L with goals 5-6.
Portugal won the first meeting 2-1 away in Oslo on September 27. João Félix and Gonçalo Ramos scored for Portugal and Erling Haaland scored for Norway.
Portugal won 4-2 away to Denmark in Copenhagen on October 1. Cancelo, Ramos, Vitinha and Félix scored.

Norway lost 2-1 to Wales on October 1 and beat Denmark 3-2 in their opening Nations League match, with Haaland scoring twice against Denmark. Parts of this preview's table look unreliable: it also lists games against Brazil and England.

Captain Cristiano Ronaldo, 41, left Portugal's camp on Wednesday, September 30, after coach Jorge Jesus said he would be benched again; he had been an unused substitute in Oslo. He will not be available against Norway. The federation said the remaining 24 players would carry on as planned.
Team news: Portugal's Francisco Conceição is doubtful with a thigh injury. Norway's Julian Ryerson is doubtful with a muscle injury and Torbjørn Heggem is suspended.
Goal.com reported that Norway captain Martin Ødegaard was seen limping after the Oslo match. AllFootball's report has a press officer pointing out that he played in the next match, against Wales.
All-time head-to-head: Portugal 9 wins, Norway 1, draws 2 across 12 matches. Recent form: Portugal W-W-W-L-W, Norway L-L-W-L-W.

Goal.com lists the last five meetings as Portugal 4 wins, Norway 1, with no draws; Norway's win was 1-0 in Euro qualifying in 2023. Some of the dates Goal.com gives are doubtful, and five matches is a small sample.

market.question: Will Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva win the 2026 Brazilian presidential election?
market.rules:
A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate that wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If the result of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

recent_facts.fact: In Datafolha's simulated runoff, Lula has 48% and Flávio Bolsonaro 45%, with blank/null at 6% and undecided at 1%. With a ±2 pt margin of error this is a technical tie. The previous Datafolha poll (Sept 24) had 47% to 45%.

AtlasIntel's Sept 29 survey has a runoff tied at 50% to 50%. Its Sept 23 survey had Lula 50.2% to Flávio 49.8% of valid votes. AtlasIntel's September first-round figures were Lula 46.2% and Flávio 43.1%.

A candidate wins in the first round only with more than half of valid votes. Otherwise the top two go to a runoff on October 25, 2026. That date is after these questions close (2026-10-05 03:59 UTC), but the markets include any runoff.

The first round is October 4, 2026, and the runoff if needed is October 25, 2026. The main candidates are Lula (PT, incumbent), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL, endorsed by imprisoned Jair Bolsonaro), Caiado (PSD), Cury (Avante) and Zema (Novo), plus seven minor candidates.

In 2022, Datafolha's final first-round poll had Lula at 50% and Bolsonaro at 36% of valid votes. The actual result was Lula 48.43% and Bolsonaro 43.20%, so polls understated the Bolsonaro side by about 7 points.

UNVERIFIED, from memory: incumbent presidents running for re-election in Brazil won 3 of 4 times: FHC in 1998, Lula in 2006 and Dilma in 2014. Bolsonaro lost in 2022, 49.1% to 50.9%. Since 1989, 7 of 9 presidential elections went to a runoff.

On September 1, leaked private messages between Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes and a banker set off an institutional crisis. Through mid-September it grew into a standoff involving several justices and the Federal Police director, overshadowing campaign coverage.

CB L'Jarius Sneed practiced fully on Friday after being limited earlier in the week. S Chamarri Conner is set to make his 2026 debut after missing Weeks 1–3. Caleb Rogers replaces Powers-Johnson at right guard for Las Vegas.

The 2026 Raiders are coached by first-year head coach Klint Kubiak, with QB Kirk Cousins, who signed in April. Their results: beat Miami 27-13, beat the Chargers 26-14 and beat New Orleans 35-27. They went 3-14 in 2025.

market.question: Will Flávio Bolsonaro finish in second place in the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election?
market.rules:
A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate who receives the second-most valid votes in the first round of this election.

The named candidates will be primarily ranked by the number of valid votes received in the specified election. If two or more candidates are tied on valid votes, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the candidates' last names. This market will resolve to the candidate that occupies the second-highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

recent_facts.fact: In the Datafolha poll released October 1 (fieldwork Sept 28–30, 2,506 interviews), Lula had 45% of valid votes in the first round and Flávio Bolsonaro had 40%. In total votes it was 42% to 38%.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate who receives the most valid votes in the first round of this election.

market.question: Will Benjamin Netanyahu be the next Prime Minister of Israel?
market.rules:
Legislative elections are schedule to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026. 

This market will resolve to the next individual who is officially appointed and sworn in as Prime Minister of Israel following the 2026 parliamentary election. If an election is called early, this market will immediately resolve to the individual who is officially appointed and sworn in after that election.

To count for resolution, the individual must be formally sworn in. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister is sworn in by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Government of Israel; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.fact: A Channel 13 poll (1,103 respondents, margin of error 2.5%) gave Netanyahu's bloc 54 seats, the Jewish opposition bloc 52 and the Arab parties 14. Party seats: Yashar (Eisenkot) 21, Likud 19, Together (Bennett) 11, Democrats (Golan) 11.
Opposition bloc leaders have said they will not form a coalition that includes Arab parties. That leaves the 14 Arab-party seats in the Channel 13 poll outside either bloc's coalition math.

A Kan 11 poll (552 respondents, margin of error 4.2%) had the Eisenkot-led bloc and Netanyahu's bloc tied at 52 seats each, with the Arab parties at 12 and the Hendel–Zelekha party at 4. Yashar had 23 seats, Likud 21 and Together 11.
Across five recent polls, Yashar averaged 23.6 seats and Likud 21.8. Yashar led in four of the five; an i24NEWS poll had Likud first with 27 seats to Yashar's 22.

As of 2026-09-15, the 15-day polling average had Likud and Yashar tied at 23.2 seats each. The parties in Netanyahu's current coalition together averaged 54.9 seats, short of the 61 needed for a majority.
Polls taken after the list-submission deadline left both blocs short of 61. One Channel 12 poll had the change bloc at 54, the current coalition at 50, the Arab parties at 12 and Hendel–Zelekha at 4.

The 26th Knesset election is set for 2026-10-27. All 120 seats are filled by proportional representation with a 3.25% threshold, and 61 seats are needed for a majority. The question closes 2026-10-28, the day after the vote.
On October 2, the Supreme Court overturned disqualifications of Ra'am, the Joint List and candidate Ofer Cassif, so these Arab lists can run.

The question resolves only to a PM formally sworn in after the 2026 election; interim or caretaker PMs do not count. Netanyahu stays caretaker PM until a new government is sworn in, and if none is sworn in by 2027-12-31 the market resolves 'Other'.

Unverified, from memory: of the five Knesset elections from April 2019 to November 2022, two (April and September 2019) produced no government and led to new elections. Netanyahu was sworn in after March 2020 (May 2020) and November 2022 (Dec 29, 2022). After March 2021, Bennett was sworn in (June 2021).
Unverified, from memory: the time from election to swearing-in has ranged from about 8 weeks (2022) to about 12 weeks (2021). No government has been sworn in within a day of the vote.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's October 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for October 27-28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The next FOMC meeting is October 27-28, 2026, and the statement comes out on October 28. If the upper bound of the range is raised from 4.00% to 4.25%, that counts as a 25 bp increase.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

If the specified candidate does not appear on the ballot in the first round, or otherwise receives no valid votes, this market will resolve to the lowest range bracket.

market.question: Will the upper bound of the federal funds rate be above 4.00% following the Fed's Oct 28, 2026 meeting? (Above 4.00%)
market.rules:
If the upper bound of the target federal funds rate published on the Federal Reserve's official website is greater than 4.00% following the Federal Reserve's Oct 28, 2026 meeting, then the market resolves to Yes.
This market will expire the first 2:05 PM ET following the release of a Federal Reserve statement for their Oct 28, 2026 meeting or one week following the last day of that meeting.

recent_facts.source: CNBC / Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta (FOMC statement)
recent_facts.fact: At its Sept 16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bp, from 3.50%-3.75% to 3.75%-4.00%. The upper bound is now exactly 4.00%, so the Oct 28 decision would have to be another hike for the upper bound to be above 4.00%.

The FOMC states the target range as a lower and upper bound, and moves usually come in 25 bp steps. Holding at 3.75%-4.00% leaves the upper bound at 4.00%, which is not above 4.00%. A 25 bp hike would raise it to 4.25%.

The September dot plot's median has the fed funds rate ending 2026 at 4.1%, which implies one more 25 bp hike this year. The median shows no change in 2027. Two FOMC meetings are left in 2026: Oct 27-28 and Dec 8-9.

September nonfarm payrolls rose just 29,000, against a consensus of about 84,000, and unemployment rose to 4.2% from 4.1%. August was revised down to +133,000, and July was revised to a loss of 10,000.
The BLS cut a combined 60,000 jobs from its July and August tallies. Those are the months whose data underpinned the Fed's Sept 16 hike.

Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and NY Fed President John Williams both said they would rather see more data before considering further action. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said 'there is plenty of room for anything to be on the table' and that inflation 'can't...get even more out of control.'
After the weak jobs report, coverage described expectations as having firmed for the Fed to hold rates at the October meeting. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has not said where he thinks rates need to go.

On Sept 29, Governor Michael Barr said he sees no clear trend toward 2% inflation and that in his base case 'further policy adjustments are likely to be needed.' Williams said the September hike removed any urgency but that one more increase 'may be appropriate late this year.' St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem did not address the rate path.

August core PCE inflation was 3.0% year on year (+0.2% m/m), and July core was revised down to 3.0% from 3.3%. Core has held at 3% for three months. Headline PCE was 3.4% y/y in August, and Q2 GDP was revised up to 2.2%.
Key data still due before the Oct 27-28 FOMC meeting is September CPI on Oct 14. The next PCE report comes out Oct 29, after the decision.
The next FOMC decision comes at the end of the Oct 27-28, 2026 meeting, with the statement usually released at 2:00 PM ET on Oct 28.

market.question: Will Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva finish in second place in the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election?
market.rules:
A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate who receives the second-most valid votes in the first round of this election.

The named candidates will be primarily ranked by the number of valid votes received in the specified election. If two or more candidates are tied on valid votes, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the candidates' last names. This market will resolve to the candidate that occupies the second-highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

recent_facts.fact: In the Datafolha poll released October 1 (fieldwork Sept 28–30, 2,506 interviews), Lula had 45% of valid votes in the first round and Flávio Bolsonaro had 40%. In total votes it was 42% to 38%.

The PoderData/Aya poll released October 3, the day before the vote, had Lula at 45% of valid votes and Flávio Bolsonaro at 43%. The margin of error is 1.5 points, so the poll describes this as a technical tie.

Vox Brasil (Sept 29–Oct 1, n=2,100) had Flávio Bolsonaro at 41.2% and Lula at 40.4%. Futura (Sept 25–29, n=2,000) had Flávio at 42.2% and Lula at 39.4%. These are the only two late-September/early-October polls in the table showing Flávio ahead.

Other recent first-round polls had Lula ahead: Real Time (Sept 26–30) 43% to 39%; Indexa (Sept 27–29) 39% to 34%; Vox Brasil (Sept 26–28) 41.4% to 37.8%; AtlasIntel (Sept 23–28, n=5,005) 45.3% to 42.2%. No other candidate exceeded about 9% combined.

Carlos Bruce took his complaint about a possible disguised re-election of López Aliaga to the OAS (Organization of American States).

Allison said that if elected he would audit López Aliaga's administration, saying there were 'very clear signs of corruption'.

market.question: Will Flávio Bolsonaro win between 36% and 39% of the valid vote in the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election?
market.rules:
A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the percentage of valid votes received by Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round of this election.

The percentage of valid votes received by the specified candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes the candidate receives in the first round by the sum of all valid votes cast in the first round.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

If the specified candidate does not appear on the ballot in the first round, or otherwise receives no valid votes, this market will resolve to the lowest range bracket.

This market will resolve based on the official vote count.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to the lowest range bracket.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, including the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

market.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by October 15, 2026?
market.rules:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

recent_facts.fact: As of the October 2 update, the US blockade of Iranian ports was still in force. Trump said on September 30 that the US had 'virtually total control', which has not been verified. The update also says no active ceasefire negotiations were confirmed as of October 3 and that Qatar is still mediating.

On October 1, Trump rejected Iran's seven-day proposal and insisted that nuclear issues be dealt with first. Iran had offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for the release of about $12 billion in frozen assets, the lifting of oil sanctions and an end to the US blockade.

A source told The National that Iran is preparing for a 'major round of fighting'. Several meetings in New York last month ended without a breakthrough, and both Trump and Iranian officials have signaled they are getting ready for the war to resume. Araghchi said Iran would fight even if it meant an 'apocalyptic' war.

Trump called the Iranian plan 'unacceptable' and described the blockade as 'the greatest blockade in military history -- it's a wall of steel'. The US sent a counterproposal. The two sides disagree on sequencing: Iran wants the US to act first, and Washington wants Iran to reopen the strait first.

Officials said mediators were working on a framework with these terms: reopen the strait with no tolls, lift the US blockade first, remove sanctions afterward, and include Iranian nuclear concessions and inspector access. Officials also said the US had not formally rejected the proposal and that Trump's public rejection may have been a negotiating tactic. Indirect talks were expected to resume on Monday, September 28.

Trump said he expected negotiations with Iran that week even though he had rejected Iran's latest proposal. That proposal was conveyed in indirect talks in New York and tied reopening Hormuz to lifting the blockade, oil-sanctions relief and a regional ceasefire.
Iran loaded no crude onto tankers in September 2026, down from about 250,000 barrels per day in August, because of the US blockade.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States naval blockade of Iran)
recent_facts.fact: The second phase of the blockade started on July 14, 2026 and is still going on. By September 12, more than 100 ships had been redirected, and several vessels had been disabled, including Belma, Lavine and Vela Nova. The article says the blockade has completely stopped new Iranian oil exports from the Gulf.

Trump said strikes could resume after the November 3 midterm elections 'if negotiations fail'. A third carrier strike group, USS Theodore Roosevelt, is heading to the CENTCOM area. No formal talks with a fixed date before October 15 were found.

Iran dismissed a 15-point US plan covering sanctions relief, nuclear rollback, missile limits and reopening Hormuz. Iran's counterproposal demands war reparations, guarantees against future war and Iranian sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz.

Precedent: the first phase of the blockade ran from April 13 to June 18, 2026, about 66 days. It was lifted the same day a US-Iran memorandum was signed (at Versailles), which extended the ceasefire and started a 60-day negotiation clock. Lifting the blockade was announced at the time the deal took effect.

Trump announced the blockade was being reinstated on July 13, less than a month into the June ceasefire. This followed Iranian attacks on commercial ships in Hormuz starting July 7, and enforcement resumed July 14. Unverified count from this research: the US has announced an end to the blockade once (June 18) and reinstated it once.

market.rules:

To count for resolution, the individual must be elected by the National Assembly and be formally sworn-in, resulting in the official formation of a new government. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister who is not elected by the National Assembly will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister takes office by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

This market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on official information from the Serbian government.

recent_facts.fact: Aleksandar Vučić resigned as President of Serbia on Sept 27, 2026. He did so to lead his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in the Oct 25 early parliamentary election as its candidate for prime minister. The constitution barred him from a third presidential term.
SNS formally proposed Vučić as its prime minister if it wins the early election. He heads the list called 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia'.

Vučić dissolved parliament and called early parliamentary elections for Oct 25, 2026. The regular election had been due by December 2027. The question closes the same day, Oct 25, 2026, which is before any new government could be elected by the Assembly.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (Opinion polling for the next Serbian parliamentary election)
recent_facts.fact: Latest poll: NSPM (fieldwork Sept 30) has the Student List at 44.4% and SNS/United Serbia at 41.7%. In the previous NSPM poll (July 30) the Student List led 39.6% to 37.5%.

Faktor Plus (fieldwork Sept 16–20, n=986) has SNS/United Serbia at 48.6%, Student List 37.1%, SPS 4.9% and European Serbia 3.6%, with 16% undecided. Its Sept 4 poll had SNS at 47.2% and the Student List at 31.5%.

All 250 Assembly seats are filled by closed-list proportional representation in one nationwide constituency, using the d'Hondt method. The threshold is 3%, and it is waived for ethnic minority lists. A government needs 126 votes in the National Assembly. 16 lists are running.

The Student List ('Students Win') says it has no leader. Dr. Ilija Srđanović is first on the list, and its candidates include Dejan Bodiroga and former central bank governor Dejan Šoškić. It has not named a prime ministerial candidate, so if it wins, the next PM would be someone other than Vučić.
Ana Brnabić, the parliament speaker and a close Vučić ally, became acting president. She must hold a presidential election within 90 days of the resignation, so no later than Dec 27, 2026.

The current prime minister is Đuro Macut, an independent who took office after Miloš Vučević resigned in January 2025. Wikipedia gives the date as April 16, 2026, which is probably a typo for 2025. Macut is not running as a PM candidate, and there is no mention of a new government being formed before the election.

Unverified, from memory: after recent Serbian elections, new governments were elected roughly 1.5 to 7 months after the vote. Examples: 2014 vote Mar 16, government Apr 27; 2016 Apr 24 to Aug 11; 2020 Jun 21 to Oct 28; 2022 Apr 3 to Oct 26; 2023 Dec 17 to May 2, 2024. SNS won the most seats in every parliamentary election from 2012 to 2023, and Vučić was elected PM in 2014 and 2016.
Polling context: before July 2026, SNS had come first in every regular national poll since July 2010. 2026 is the first election cycle in which polls are split on who will finish first.

recent_facts.fact: The September 2025 CPI-U NSA index was 324.800, up 3.0% y/y. That puts the Aug-to-Sep 2025 NSA rise at about +0.25%, from 323.976. This is the base the September 2026 y/y figure is measured against.

recent_facts.source: Derived arithmetic from BLS index levels
recent_facts.fact: For the published y/y to round to 3.7% or higher, the September 2026 NSA index must exceed about 336.655 (324.800 × 1.0365). That requires an Aug-to-Sep 2026 NSA rise of about +0.50% from 334.980. A rise of about +0.40% (index about 336.33) would give roughly 3.55–3.6%. A rise near +0.25%, the same as last September, would leave y/y near 3.4%.
In August 2026, gasoline rose 3.9% m/m (SA) and 27.4% y/y, and energy rose 2.1% m/m and 16.3% y/y. Core CPI rose 0.3% m/m and 2.4% y/y, and food rose 0.1% m/m and 2.7% y/y.
Gasoline accounted for over one third of the 0.4% monthly all-items increase in August 2026.
EIA monthly average U.S. regular retail gasoline: June 2026 $4.050, July $3.932, August $4.058, September $4.355. That makes September about 7.3% above August.

AAA's September 2026 monthly average gas price was $4.33, a record for September and 50 cents above the previous record of $3.83 set in 2023. The national average was $4.41 on Oct 1, down nearly 7 cents in a week, and crude was in the $90/barrel range.
AAA's national average climbed through September 2026: $4.14 on Sep 3, $4.27 on Sep 10, $4.43 on Sep 17 and $4.48 on Sep 24, the highest ever for that time of year.

AAA reported August 2026 as the most expensive August on record, with the national average above $4 every day. The mid-month August average was $4.06, and a secondary summary gave $4.19 for the full month; the two AAA-derived figures disagree, so this one is unverified.
September 2026 CPI is scheduled for release on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET, which is 12:30 UTC. The question closes at 12:29 UTC that day.
The question resolves on the one-decimal 12-month NSA all-items CPI-U change BLS reports for September 2026. It must be strictly above 3.6%, so 3.6% resolves No and 3.7% or higher resolves Yes.

market.question: Will Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva win the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election by less than 5%?
market.rules:
A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the first round of the next Brazil Presidential Election.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the vote count has been made official.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).
